title: stale-row-log@1
description: One cleanup log record of the VPS watchdog (stale-row@1): what it did to one stale row and why (Brett, Nov 16 2026: "I want a server fucking watchdog on the VPS to do that."). framework/core/stale-rows.mjs is the reference classifier; a record is its verdict on one row plus where the row lives, when, and who ran it. Appended to the cleanup log, never edited.

id.description: <kind>:<rowId>:<at>: stable, so a replayed log gives each record once

rowId.description: the row's id where it lives: build id, PR number (merge queue), UI Review item id

build.description: the build the row is or points at ('' when none)

pr.description: the PR the row carries (0 = none)

evidence.description: every fact the rule used, in plain words (PR #12 merged 2026-11-16 (abc123); on main by squash; build x: complete)

by.description: watchdog, or who ran it by hand (cli:<who>, console:<who>)

dry.description: true = decided, not applied (a dry run)

action.description: keep = the row stays; complete = the work landed on main, the row is marked done where it lives (build → complete, merge-queue entry → landed, UI Review item → landed, never approved); remove = the work is dead, the row leaves the list (build → archived, entry / item → removed)

reason.description: keep: invalid-row, live, own-status, no-facts, open · complete: pr-merged, on-main, build-complete · remove: pr-closed, build-failed, build-cancelled. Open registry: add a code, never reuse one.

facts.title: stale-row-facts@1
facts.description: What the watchdog looked up for one row before classifying it. Every piece nullable: null = not looked up, never a claim.
